To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Taxol causes the serine phosphorylation and electrophoretic retardation of the 66 kDa Shc isoforms in human A549 lung carcinoma cells.

the 66-kD Shc isoform undergoes Taxol-induced serinethreonine phosphorylation in the human lung carcinoma cells A549, and that this modification is associated with the mitotic arrest induced by microtubule-active compounds.
the 66-kD isoform of the adapter protein Shc undergoes a serine phosphorylation that results in an altered mobility on SDS-PAGE in cells treated with microtubule-disrupting agents.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a new signaling event in Taxol-treated cells that may be involved in the mechanism of Taxol-induced apoptosis.
the identification of the signaling events that lead from Taxol exposure to cell death.
the identification of a novel serine phosphorylation site of the 66- kDa Shc isoforms that is induced by microtubule- interacting drugs and may be a potential target of Taxol-induced apoptosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Taxol causes a decrease in electrophoretic migration of Shc p66, which is due to serine phosphorylation.
the electrophoretic shift of Shc induced by Taxol is due to serine phosphorylation and may be an important event in the signaling pathways that result in cell death.
Taxol induces serine phosphorylation in the 66-kD Shc isoform, and this may be a result of an MEK-independent signaling event.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Taxol mediates a serine phosphorylation event in the Shc protein, which is not a consequence of a Grb2/Shc complex, and which may play a role as part of a signaling pathway that leads to Taxol-induced cell death.
the Taxol-induced serinethreonine phosphorylation of Shc is a novel mechanism that is associated with the microtubuleinteracting drugs, is MEK-independent, and is a possible mechanism of cell death.
Taxol induces serine phosphorylation and a concomitant decreased electrophoretive mobility shift of the 66 kDa isoform of Shc.
The main takeaway from our work is that

microtubule-disrupting drugs cause a serine phosphorylation and a decrease in electrophoretic migration of the 66 kDa Shc isoforms (p66Shc) in human lung adenocarcinoma A549 cells, but not in Taxol-resistant variant cells.
Taxol causes a serine phosphorylation and a subsequent electrophoretic shift of the 66 kDa Shc isoforms in the human lung carcinoma A549 cells.
Taxol-induced ser/thr phosphorylation of p66shcs is a common feature in microtubule interacting drugs.
